stations.title: Ambrose
stations.say: Why do I keep writing this twice?

stations.title: Two functions
stations.text: One for tickets, one for bills, alike.

captions: Ambrose has the same function twice, and Dorrit wants a third copy for her deposits.
A fix in one copy never reaches the other, so the copies drift apart.
You write the function once, with the type left open, and keep quotes in range with it.
Dorrit's deposits use the same recipe, and nothing is written a third time.
One recipe serves every list in the workshop. Next, a whole class with its type left open.
